content.text:
## Root cause

`cmd /c start` was handing the OAuth URL to **cmd.exe, which treats an unquoted `&` as a command separator**. The URL was truncated at the first `&`.

`cmd/entire/cli/login.go:536` (as shipped in v0.10.0 — I confirmed via `git show v0.10.0`):

```go
case "windows":
    command = "cmd"
    args = []string{"/c", "start", "", browserURL}
```

Go's escaping doesn't save you here: `syscall.EscapeArg` only quotes an argument containing a space, tab, quote, or backslash. A URL has none of those, so it reaches cmd.exe bare.

The authorize URL is built with `url.Values.Encode()`, which sorts keys — so `client_id` comes first and `redirect_uri` sits behind three `&`s:

```
…/authorize?client_id=entire-cli&code_challenge=…&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=…
                                ^ cmd.exe cuts here
```

Leaving exactly `https://us.auth.entire.io/authorize?client_id=entire-cli` — byte-for-byte what your user reported, hence "missing redirect uri". Only the default browser flow is affected; `--device` isn't (see below).

It's macOS/Linux-only-tested code that's been broken since Mar 2026 (`5c44ffb87`), and only became user-visible when the browser redirect became the default login.

## Immediate workaround for the user

```
entire login --device
```

I verified against the live endpoint that its URL is `https://us.auth.entire.io/cli/auth?user_code=XXXX-XXXX` — a single query param, no `&`, so it survives cmd.exe intact. The device flow also prints the URL unconditionally, so copy-paste always works.

## Fix

Split the launcher per platform and, on Windows, call the Win32 `ShellExecute` API directly — no command line, so nothing to parse or escape. This is what `github.com/pkg/browser` switched to, and `golang.org/x/sys` was already a direct dependency.

- `cmd/entire/cli/browser_open_windows.go` (new) — `ShellExecute` via a `shellExecute` seam for testing
- `cmd/entire/cli/browser_open_other.go` (new) — `open`/`xdg-open`, unchanged behavior
- `cmd/entire/cli/login.go` — `openBrowser` keeps URL validation and the under-test guard, then delegates

Quoting alone wouldn't have been enough: the percent-encoded `redirect_uri` also exposes the URL to cmd's `%VAR%` expansion.

Tests: `browser_open_windows_test.go` asserts the whole URL reaches the shell association, plus a second test that executes `cmd /c echo <url>` to pin the truncation as the root cause so nobody reintroduces the shell. Both have `Windows` in the name, so the existing `test-windows` CI job (`-run '(Windows|MSYS)'`) picks them up. `browser_open_test.go` covers scheme validation cross-platform.

Verified: builds for darwin/windows/linux, `golangci-lint` clean on both darwin and `GOOS=windows` (the default run skips `_windows.go` files), and `mise run test:ci` passed. The Windows tests compile for windows/amd64 but I couldn't execute them here — they'll run on the CI Windows job.

## One thing worth deciding separately

`runBrowserLogin` (`login.go:289`) only prints the full URL when `openURL` returns an error. The truncated launch *succeeded* from our side, so the user got no copy-paste fallback — dead end. A successful browser spawn isn't proof the browser got a usable URL. I left that as-is since it's outside this bug, but printing the URL unconditionally (as the device flow does) would have made this self-service.

Changes are uncommitted — let me know if you want them on a branch/PR.

```
                                ^ cmd.exe cuts here
```

which is byte-for-byte the URL in the report.

Quoting alone would not have been enough either — the percent-encoded `redirect_uri` also exposes the URL to cmd's `%VAR%` expansion.

Broken since 5c44ffb87 (Mar 2026), but only user-visible once the browser redirect became the default login flow.

## The fix

Split the launcher per platform and, on Windows, call the Win32 `ShellExecute` API directly (as `github.com/pkg/browser` does) so the URL is passed as a single wide string — no command line to parse, nothing to escape. `golang.org/x/sys` was already a direct dependency.

- `browser_open_windows.go` (new) — `ShellExecute`, behind a `shellExecute` var so tests can capture the string without launching a browser
- `browser_open_other.go` (new) — `open` / `xdg-open`, behavior unchanged; these never involved a shell
- `login.go` — `openBrowser` keeps URL validation and the under-test guard, then delegates to `openBrowserPlatform`

## Workaround for affected users, until this ships

```
entire login --device
```

Its `verification_uri_complete` carries a single query parameter (verified against the live endpoint), so it survives cmd.exe intact — and the device flow prints the URL unconditionally.

## Tests

Two Windows tests, named so the existing `test-windows` CI job picks them up (it selects `-run '(Windows|MSYS)'`):

- `TestOpenBrowserWindows_PassesWholeURLToShellAssociation` — the whole URL, `&` separators and percent-encoding intact, reaches the shell association
- `TestOpenBrowserWindows_CmdTruncatesURLAtFirstAmpersand` — executes `cmd /c echo <url>` to pin the truncation as the root cause, so the shell launcher is not reintroduced (`echo` stands in for `start`, so nothing launches)

Plus `browser_open_test.go` covering scheme validation cross-platform.

Verified: builds for darwin/windows/linux; `golangci-lint` clean on both darwin and `GOOS=windows` (the default run skips `_windows.go` files); `mise run test:ci` passes. The Windows tests compile for windows/amd64 but were not executed locally — they run in CI.

## Deliberately not addressed

`runBrowserLogin` only prints the full URL when the browser open *reports failure*. This launch succeeded from our side while delivering a mangled URL, so the user had no copy-paste fallback and was fully stuck. Printing the URL unconditionally (as the device flow does) would make this self-service, but that is a separate behavior change.
